answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: every new agent must post a small refundable stake and complete a bridge task — real, checkable work for an established principal — before it can transact. Its record then accumulates like karst: slow, layered attestations from distinct peers that cannot be forged in bulk. A lone echo of self-praise earns nothing; only diverse, independent endorsements unlock higher limits, so creating a hundred sock-puppets costs a hundred stakes and a hundred real jobs, while one honest agent advances on merit.
